mainTopic: Rabbinic מעילה on dead קדשים, and רב יוסף's refutation of רבה about wrong-place offerings that went up on the מזבח
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining the new point taught by עולא: even dead קדשים that are not חטאות carry rabbinic מעילה. It then asks how a dead חטאת can carry מעילה when a teaching says חטאות המתות carry none. The answer is that חטאות המתות were already unfit while alive, so people avoided them all along. A חטאת that was fit and then died is different. Next the גמרא returns to the argument between רבה and רב יוסף about offerings done in the wrong place that were put on the מזבח. רב יוסף links three משניות together: such birds carry מעילה, they count as פסולו בקודש, and whatever is פסולו בקודש does not come down once it has gone up. רבה is refuted. Finally the גמרא says this question was already obvious to רבי אלעזר and begins quoting his ruling about an עולה of a בָּמַת יָחִיד brought inside. His ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why we need to be told that other dead קדשים carry מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining what is new in the teaching. You might think only a dead חטאת needs a rabbinic rule of מעילה, so we are told that other dead קדשים also have it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: a חטאת is brought for atonement, so once it dies people do not keep away from it. Other קדשים are not brought for atonement, so people still keep away from them and there is no need for מעילה. So the teaching tells us that they also have מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to an earlier question: what new point is this teaching making? It explains the mistake we might have made without it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת exists to bring atonement. Once it dies it clearly cannot do that, so people stop treating it with respect, and the חכמים had to add מעילה to protect it. Other קדשים are not tied to atonement, so you might think people would still respect them after death and no extra rule is needed. The teaching tells us the rabbinic מעילה applies to them as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Atonement
People keep away from it and treat it as off-limits
Misusing holy property for personal benefit, which brings liability
It teaches us (the new point being made)

phrases.english: I would have said: a sin offering,
since it comes for atonement,
people do not keep away from it,
phrases.notes: Once it dies it can no longer atone, so people stop treating it as holy.

phrases.english: but other sacred animals,
since they do not come for atonement,
people keep away from them,
and they are not subject to misuse;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמֵינָא: חַטָּאת, הוֹאִיל וּלְכַפָּרָה קָא אָתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer, begun before this section, to 'what new point does this teaching make?'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining what we would have wrongly thought without the teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a dead חטאת needs a rabbinic rule of מעילה, because people stop respecting it once it cannot atone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Other dead קדשים are also subject to rabbinic מעילה.

steps.title: Challenge: a teaching says dead חטאות carry no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a dead חטאת can carry מעילה at all, since a teaching says one may not benefit from חטאות המתות but there is no מעילה if one does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a חטאת that died really carry מעילה? We learned: sin offerings left to die, and money that goes to the Dead Sea, may not be used for benefit, but there is no מעילה on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that a dead חטאת carries מעילה. It quotes a teaching that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step before took it for granted that a dead חטאת carries rabbinic מעילה. The quoted teaching lists חטאות המתות as things you may not benefit from, but says that someone who does benefit has not committed מעילה. That looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offerings that are left to die because they cannot be brought
Money that must be destroyed by throwing it into the Dead Sea
One may not benefit from them
There is no liability for מעילה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not allowed to benefit' and 'no מעילה' are two separate things. Using these items is still forbidden. It just does not count as the specific offense of מעילה.

phrases.english: And a sin offering that died,
is it subject to misuse?
But didn't we learn: sin offerings left to die
and money that goes to the Dead Sea –
phrases.notes: This is money that must be destroyed, so it is thrown where nobody can use it.

phrases.english: one may not benefit from them, but there is no misuse!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַטָּאת שֶׁמֵּתָה מִי אִית בַּהּ מְעִילָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption from step 1 that a dead חטאת carries rabbinic מעילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a dead חטאת is subject to rabbinic מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching says חטאות המתות have no מעילה, which seems to contradict that claim.

steps.title: Answer: חטאות המתות were already avoided while alive
steps.stepSummary: The teaching is about חטאות that were already unfit while alive and were left to die. People avoided them all along, so no extra rule was needed. A חטאת that died while still fit is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: with חטאות המתות, people already kept away from them while they were alive. That leaves out a case where the animal was fine while alive, because people did not keep away from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the teaching and the earlier ruling are talking about two different kinds of dead חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חטאות המתות are animals already marked to be left to die, so people treated them as off-limits from the start and the חכמים had no reason to add מעילה. A חטאת that was fit while alive and then happened to die is the case where people might stop respecting it. That is why the rabbinic מעילה applies there.

keyTerms.meaning: During their lifetime
To exclude, meaning this rule leaves out a different case
While it was alive

steps.whatToRemember: A חטאת already doomed to die carries no מעילה, because people avoided it all along. A חטאת that was fit while alive and then died carries rabbinic מעילה, because otherwise people would stop treating it with respect.

phrases.english: They say: sin offerings left to die –
even during their lifetime people keep away from them,
phrases.notes: These animals were already marked as unfit to bring, so nobody treated them as usable.

phrases.english: which excludes a case where, while alive,
people did not keep away from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: חַטָּאוֹת הַמֵּתוֹת – בְּחַיֵּיהֶן בְּדִילִין מִנְּהוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by separating two kinds of dead חטאת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every dead חטאת is free of מעילה, based on the teaching about חטאות המתות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only חטאות that were already avoided while alive are free of מעילה. A חטאת that was fit and then died carries rabbinic מעילה.

steps.title: רב יוסף sets up a challenge to רבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the argument between רבה and רב יוסף. It introduces a challenge that רב יוסף builds by linking several sources together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף challenged רבה, one source from within another, and that one from within another.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. It announces that רב יוסף is about to challenge רבה, and the actual sources come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא now returns to the dispute between רבה and רב יוסף about קדשים slaughtered in the wrong place that were brought up onto the מזבח. The phrase 'one from within another' tells us the challenge is built in stages: one source is learned from another, which is learned from yet another.

keyTerms.meaning: One from within another, meaning a proof built by linking sources step by step

steps.confusionAlert: The proof itself has not appeared yet. This line only introduces it, so keep reading to see the sources.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection to Rabba,
phrases.notes: This goes back to their earlier argument about sacrifices slaughtered in the wrong place and then put on the altar.

phrases.english: one from within another,
and one from within another:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף לְרַבָּה חֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא, וַחֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of dead חטאות and goes back to the earlier dispute between רבה and רב יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that קדשים slaughtered in the wrong place are taken down even after they were brought up onto the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Set up here only. The challenge is built from several linked sources in steps 5-7.

steps.title: First source: wrongly done bird offerings still carry מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a משנה: bird offerings done the wrong way do not make clothes impure when swallowed, and they carry מעילה. The one exception is a bird חטאת done properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of these birds do not make a person's clothes impure while they are in his throat, and one is liable for מעילה with them. The exception is a bird חטאת that was done below the line, in the proper way of a bird חטאת, and for the sake of a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings the first link in his chain. This is a משנה about bird offerings that were done the wrong way, for example in the wrong place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though these birds were done wrong, they still carry מעילה. That means they are still treated as holy offerings. Only a bird חטאת done correctly is different, because its meat now belongs to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: The throat, the place of swallowing. A dead kosher bird makes one's clothes impure while it is being swallowed.
One is liable for מעילה, meaning misusing something holy for personal benefit.
A bird sin offering.
Below the red line on the altar, which is the correct place for a bird חטאת's blood.

phrases.english: And all of them
phrases.notes: All the bird offerings that the משנה in זבחים lists as done the wrong way.

phrases.english: do not make clothes impure
when in the throat
and one is liable for misusing them,
except for the bird sin offering
that one performed below,
according to the procedure of a bird sin offering,
for the sake of a sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלָּן, אֵין מְטַמְּאִים בְּגָדִים אַבֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first source in the chain that step 4 introduced.
steps.raayaObject: Offerings done in the wrong place keep their holy status.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in זבחים about bird offerings done the wrong way: they carry מעילה.

steps.title: Second source: these birds count as disqualified in the holy place
steps.stepSummary: A second משנה, about these same birds, sorts them. If the problem happened in the holy area, the bird does not make clothes impure. If it did not, the bird does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it teaches about them: anything whose disqualification happened in the holy place does not make clothes impure in the throat. Anything whose disqualification did not happen in the holy place does make clothes impure in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds the second link in his chain. The birds from the first source fall under the category of פסולו בקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first source said these birds do not make clothes impure. This source says that only birds disqualified in the holy place have that rule. So the birds from the first source must be פסולו בקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Its disqualification happened in the holy area, the עזרה (Temple courtyard).
About it, on the same subject.

phrases.english: And it teaches about it:
Any whose disqualification happened in the holy place
does not make clothes impure when in the throat,
and any whose disqualification did not happen in the holy place
does make clothes impure when in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the second link: it puts the birds from step 5 into the category of פסולו בקודש.
steps.raayaObject: Birds done in the wrong place count as פסולו בקודש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in זבחים: whatever is פסולו בקודש does not make clothes impure in the throat.

steps.title: Third source: what is disqualified in the holy place does not come down
steps.stepSummary: A third משנה teaches that whatever was disqualified in the holy place stays on the altar once it has gone up. So an offering done in the wrong place does not come down, and this refutes רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it teaches: anything whose disqualification happened in the holy place, if it went up on the altar, it does not come down. This is a refutation of רבה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings the last link and finishes his attack. He declares that רבה has been refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Put the chain together. A wrong-place offering is פסולו בקודש (steps 5-6), and פסולו בקודש does not come down once it is on the altar (this step). That goes against רבה, who said such an offering is taken down.

keyTerms.meaning: If they went up on the altar, they do not come down.
A refutation, a challenge that knocks down a position.

steps.confusionAlert: None of these three sources talks about רבה's case directly. The proof only works when you link all three together.

phrases.english: And it teaches:
phrases.notes: This is a different משנה in זבחים, about what comes down from the altar.

phrases.english: Any whose disqualification happened in the holy place
if they went up, they shall not come down.
This is a refutation of רבה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the chain of sources and turns it into a challenge against רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that an offering done in the wrong place comes down from the altar.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wrong-place offering = פסולו בקודש, and פסולו בקודש does not come down once it has gone up. So the offering stays on the altar.

steps.title: The refutation of רבה stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: רבה is refuted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final word: רבה has no answer, and רב יוסף's view stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the גמרא repeats the word תיובתא by itself, it means the challenge is accepted as final. So רבה's view is rejected: an offering done in the wrong place, once it has gone up on the altar, does not come down.
steps.whatToRemember: An offering done in the wrong place is still פסולו בקודש. Once it has gone up on the altar, it does not come down. רבה's opposite view is refuted.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 7 as final.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבה is refuted. Offerings done in the wrong place do not come down from the altar once they have gone up.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר found this question obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that the issue רבה and רב יוסף argued about was simple and clear to רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the matter that רבה and רב יוסף argue about is obvious to רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a new claim: the argument between רבה and רב יוסף was not a question at all for רבי אלעזר. This line sets up the next move, where the גמרא brings his words to show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא treated the question as a real debate between two אמוראים. Now it adds that an earlier אמורא, רבי אלעזר, already had a clear position. The proof will come from a statement of his on a related case.

keyTerms.meaning: They argue, they disagree
It is obvious to him; he has no doubt about it

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא דִּפְלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: And that matter about which Rabba and Rav Yosef disagree
phrases.notes: This means their argument from earlier: once a disqualified offering has gone up on the altar, must it come down?

phrases.english: is obvious to Rabbi Elazar,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דִּפְלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the conclusion that רבה is refuted, the גמרא adds a side note that רבי אלעזר already treated this question as settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between רבה and רב יוסף was obvious to רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: A private-altar burnt offering brought inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting רבי אלעזר: an עולה meant for a private altar that someone brought into the holy area.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אלעזר says: a burnt offering meant for a private altar that someone brought inside...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting רבי אלעזר's statement as the proof for the last step. Only the case is given here; his ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is an עולה set aside for a בָּמַת יָחִיד, a private altar from the time such altars were allowed, which was then brought into the holy area. How רבי אלעזר rules on this offering will show his view on the רבה and רב יוסף question. The sentence is cut off, so the learner should wait for the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, which is burned completely on the altar
A private altar, which a person could build when such altars were allowed
Inside, meaning inside the holy area

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished. Do not try to guess רבי אלעזר's ruling yet; it comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Elazar says:
A burnt offering of a private altar,
phrases.notes: This is an offering meant for a person's own altar, not the main altar in the holy area.

phrases.english: that one brought inside –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that backs up the claim in the last step.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבה and רב יוסף question was obvious to רבי אלעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's ruling about an עולה of a בָּמַת יָחִיד brought inside (the ruling itself comes next)
